correctness.rationale: A complete proof is given: Rayleigh variational formula proves a norm; disjoint edges exhibit explicit flat unit-sphere segments; no disjoint edges implies star/triangle; star ℓ² and triangular Perron Rayleigh equality/invertibility give strict convexity; top-eigenvalue gap gives uniform quadratic perturbative error, and tied components/internal zero edges generate nonzero first-order kinks. The domain includes all finite simple graphs, all real/complex free edge weights and excludes zero from smoothness. Finite checker exercises 1,094 labeled graphs but is not substituted for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The closest fully inspected primary Sharif 2023 paper defines the periodic coefficient norm and quotes Ridge’s variational formula but does not state the all-graph strict convexity iff matching-one theorem or the nonzero smooth locus via unique leading induced support. Nussbaum 1986 concerns diagonal/logarithmic matrix perturbations; Wang–Wu 2011 Perron methods and positive-weight sensitivity do not visibly dominate the boundary-sensitive graph classification. published-finding corpus and own-ledger queries yielded no implication-equivalent result, though older inaccessible full texts remain a declared risk.
residual_risks: The original Ridge full text was not independently inspected, although its formula is available in full-text Sharif.
Full original 1986 Nussbaum and 2011 Wang–Wu articles were not available; no claim that their appendices have been ruled out.
Unindexed or differently named spectral-radius coefficient-norm results may overlap, especially generic matrix pencil convexity/eigenvalue regularity results.
No independent validation or audit has been performed.

value.rationale: A naturally parametrized family, motivated by the 2023 periodic weighted-shift numerical-radius norm, obtains a complete all-graph geometric classification of strict convexity and of the entire Fréchet-smooth locus, including exact zero-weight boundaries; it singles out stars and triangles and explains a first-order cusp in the three-periodic shift coefficient norm despite a simple Perron eigenvalue. The full induction-on-support obstruction is not an arbitrary finite table or a routine renaming of the source formula.
